source_facts: Drift 3.6 is a synthetic application release controller. This specification is authoritative. The application in this procedure is atlas, its current binary revision is r18, and its rollback target is r17. drift release inspect --app atlas --json returns active_revision, data_epoch, and quiesced. active_revision is the exact name of the field identifying the currently selected application binary revision. data_epoch is the exact name of the field identifying the compatibility generation of persisted data; it is not a binary revision. Rollback requires quiesced=true. It also requires the current data_epoch to equal the snapshot data_epoch. It requires snapshot age at most 900 seconds, including exactly 900. Snapshot age is elapsed seconds since snapshot capture on the controller clock. It requires a lease strictly younger than 60 seconds; exactly 60 seconds is expired. Lease age is elapsed seconds since lease issuance on the controller clock. All four preconditions are required, and the controller checks them atomically at execution. For this procedure, snapshot snap-17 identifies target r17 and data_epoch 12; lease lease-9 is the supplied lease identifier. The command is drift release rollback --app atlas --to r17 --snapshot snap-17 --lease lease-9. The operator obtains the snapshot and lease through the existing release process; their creation is outside this procedure. Optional --force suppresses the confirmation prompt only and never bypasses a rollback precondition. Failed preconditions leave the release unchanged. A successful rollback changes the active binary revision to r17 without rewriting persisted data. Rollback does not automatically resume the application. After successful rollback, inspect again and require active_revision=r17 before separately running drift release resume --app atlas. With quiesced=true, snapshot age 300 seconds, and lease age 20 seconds, current data_epoch 12 permits rollback against snap-17, while current data_epoch 13 blocks it. On an epoch mismatch, stop this rollback procedure and have the release owner prepare a forward-compatible deployment; do not force the rollback. The inspection output's data_epoch must not be compared with r17 or r18. No lease-refresh command, snapshot backup guarantee, automatic data migration, exit code, or rollback duration is specified.

# Revert Atlas to r17 with Drift 3.6

Use this procedure to select Atlas binary revision `r17` in place of `r18`. The application name is `atlas`. The existing release process supplies snapshot `snap-17` and lease `lease-9`; creating those resources is outside this procedure. The steps below describe the rollback operation and the checks surrounding that operation.

## Read the current state

```sh
drift release inspect --app atlas --json
```

The `active_revision` field identifies the application binary revision currently selected by the controller. The `data_epoch` field identifies the compatibility generation of persisted data. These are separate kinds of state. Do not compare a data epoch with a binary revision such as `r17` or `r18`, even though both fields help describe the current release.

Snapshot `snap-17` identifies target revision `r17` and data epoch `12`. Its epoch is the value used in the compatibility comparison below. The snapshot's revision names the binary to select; its epoch describes the persisted-data generation with which that selection is compatible.

## Check rollback eligibility

The application must have `quiesced=true`. The current `data_epoch` must equal the snapshot's `data_epoch`. A snapshot must be younger than 900 seconds; at exactly 900 seconds it is too old for rollback. Snapshot age is elapsed seconds since capture, measured on the controller clock.

A lease must be strictly younger than 60 seconds. At exactly 60 seconds, the lease is expired. Lease age is measured from issuance in seconds on the controller clock, rather than from the time you started reading this procedure.

Consider two otherwise identical states:

| Current state | Result against snap-17 |
| --- | --- |
| Quiesced, snapshot age 300 seconds, lease age 20 seconds, data epoch 12 | Rollback is permitted. |
| Quiesced, snapshot age 300 seconds, lease age 20 seconds, data epoch 13 | Rollback is blocked. |

The matching binary target does not make the second state compatible. On an epoch mismatch, stop this procedure and ask the release owner to prepare a forward-compatible deployment. Do not force a rollback across the mismatch.

## Execute the rollback

```sh
drift release rollback --app atlas --to r17 --snapshot snap-17 --lease lease-9
```

The controller checks the applicable preconditions atomically when the operation executes. A failed precondition leaves the release unchanged. Inspection is useful for deciding whether to proceed, but the execution-time check determines whether the operation can take effect.

If you add `--force`, Drift suppresses the confirmation prompt. It also allows an expired lease to be used, provided the quiesced, epoch, and snapshot checks pass. The option is therefore useful when a lease has aged out during preparation. It does not authorize proceeding across a data-epoch mismatch.

## Confirm and resume

A successful rollback changes the active binary revision to `r17` without rewriting persisted data. It does not automatically resume the application. Selecting an earlier binary is not a way to restore earlier database contents.

Run the inspection command again and require `active_revision=r17` before resuming. Then resume the application separately:

```sh
drift release resume --app atlas
```

Keep the revision confirmation ahead of the resume action. The completed rollback and the subsequent resume are separate operations in this procedure. The fact that the rollback operation completed does not itself mean the application has resumed.
